page: The Google Cloud Platform c4-highcpu-4 is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and operates on the x86_64 architecture. The CPU features a large 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated matrix operations.

Benchmark evaluations indicate highly polarized performance. The instance excels in single-core workloads, achieving top-tier results in Geekbench single-core and text processing tests, alongside strong performance in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, multi-core and memory-bound operations show significant performance degradation. Multi-core stress-ng, Passmark CPU, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression benchmarks fall into the bottom 25% tier. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with Passmark memory scores in the bottom 10% and uncached read/write memory bandwidth classified as weak.

From a resource allocation perspective, the c4-highcpu-4 offers a cost-efficient profile for workloads that demand high single-thread CPU performance but have minimal memory footprints. The inclusion of AMX and AVX-512 instructions provides high compute density for specialized vector and integer math without the overhead of larger memory configurations. However, the low memory-to-vCPU ratio and poor memory bandwidth make it poorly suited for memory-intensive databases, large-scale software compilation, or heavy multi-threaded processing. Recommended workloads include lightweight web serving, single-threaded text processing, and small-scale machine learning inference tasks that fit within the 8 GB memory limit.
